look: Photoreal, cinematic, fictional Indian cast. Night, monsoon, Mumbai-like city. Crime/con tone (Series 1).
style_block: STYLE: Photorealistic live-action film still, a single frame from a contemporary Indian crime thriller shot on a full-frame digital cinema camera. Vertical 9:16 portrait composition. Night, about 2 am, heavy monsoon rain, inside an old black-and-yellow city taxi parked under a concrete flyover in a Mumbai-like city. Real-looking fictional Indian people with natural, un-retouched skin: visible pores, fine lines, a damp sheen, no beauty smoothing. Lighting is motivated and low-key only: warm sodium-orange street light (about 2000 K) through the rain-streaked windscreen from the front right is the key; red and blue neon from a shuttered shop on the kerb side, smeared through the wet left-side windows, is the rim and fill; shadows fall to deep teal-black but keep detail; no studio fill, no flat even lighting. The only extra light sources allowed are the ones the shot description names (the green glow of a phone screen, white headlights through the rear window). Colour grade: deep teal shadows against orange and red highlights, muted mid-tone saturation, skin stays a true warm brown, blacks very slightly lifted. Lens: spherical prime look, 35 mm for wider cabin shots, 50 mm for mediums, 85 mm for close-ups, near f/2 with shallow depth of field, soft round bokeh from raindrops on glass, gentle halation around bright lights, slight natural vignette. Camera at seated eye level inside the cramped cabin, steady framing, level horizon, no wide-angle distortion. Fine 35 mm film grain over the whole frame. Rain is always present: beads and runnels on every window, wet reflections on vinyl, leather and skin. Composed for vertical video: one clear subject, the main face in the upper-middle of the frame, the bottom fifth of the frame free of faces and essential action, and a little spare picture on all four edges so the frame can be slowly pushed in or panned.
negative_rules: AVOID: No text of any kind anywhere in the image: no captions, subtitles, titles, labels, signage lettering, number plates, permit stickers, meter digits, phone-screen characters, readable newsprint or headlines; any printed surface is blurred or illegible. No watermarks, signatures, logos, brand names, borders, frames or split panels. No real company, bank, police, government or taxi-union insignia or emblems, no flags, no real or recognisable people. No extra people beyond those named in the shot, no faces in other vehicles. Do not change any character's face, age, skin tone, hair, wardrobe or jewellery from the reference sheet; do not add earrings, bindi, glasses, cap, watch, rings, moustache or beard. Right-hand-drive car only: the steering wheel and the driver are on the right side of the car. No extra, missing or fused fingers, no distorted hands, no duplicated limbs. No illustration, anime, cartoon, 3D render, CGI gloss, HDR glow, plastic skin, beauty filter or over-saturated colour. No daylight, no dry windows, no weapons, no blood.

characters.name: Tara Sethi
characters.sheet_prompt: Use your image generation tool to create ONE new vertical 9:16 image. It is a photorealistic character reference sheet (a casting and costume continuity sheet) showing one fictional Indian woman, the same person three times, on a plain seamless mid-grey studio background, lit by soft, even, neutral white studio light with no coloured light and no hard shadows, photographed like a real person on a full-frame camera with an 85 mm lens: photorealistic, natural un-retouched skin with visible pores and fine lines, not an illustration, not a 3D render. LAYOUT: three views placed on ONE continuous grey backdrop and separated only by empty grey space; the two face views are not inset photographs, not panels and not boxes, they have no rectangular edges, and the same grey backdrop runs unbroken behind and between all three views. (1) the left 45 percent of the image, full height: full-body front view, standing straight and facing the camera, arms relaxed at her sides with both hands visible, from the top of her head to her shoes fully inside the frame, with a clear margin of empty grey between her elbows and the left edge of the image and between her and the other views; (2) upper right, the largest view: a front-on face close-up from collarbone to the top of her hair, eyes into the lens, neutral expression, mouth closed; (3) lower right: head-and-shoulders three-quarter view, her head turned about 45 degrees towards her own right so that the left side of her face, her exposed left ear and the nose stud are clearly visible, eyes looking past the camera. THE WOMAN: Tara, 31 years old, about 165 cm tall, lean build, warm brown skin, an angular oval face with sharp high cheekbones, a defined jawline, a straight narrow nose, dark brown almond-shaped eyes, straight thick black eyebrows, natural lips with no lipstick. HAIR: straight black hair cut to the shoulders, damp from rain with a few wet strands clinging together, with a clean side parting on her LEFT side: the parting line sits above her left eye, which is on the viewer's RIGHT in the two front views, and from it the hair sweeps across the top of her head towards her right; the short left side is tucked behind her left ear so that ear is fully exposed, the fuller right side hangs loose to the shoulder. The parting, the tucked ear and the nose stud are all on the same side of her head, her left, in all three views. MAKE-UP: black kajal lining both eyes, slightly smudged under the lower lids; nothing else. JEWELLERY: one small plain round gold stud in her left nostril (on the viewer's right in the two front views); one thin plain gold chain lying at the collarbone with no pendant; nothing else: no earrings, no rings, no bangles, no watch, no bindi. Nails short and unpainted. WARDROBE: a charcoal-grey fitted single-breasted blazer with notch lapels and one button, worn open, its shoulders and upper sleeves visibly darker and wet from rain; under it a maroon silk pullover blouse with a soft V neckline and no collar, tucked in; the front of the blouse is one plain smooth piece of draped silk with no buttons, no button placket, no centre seam and no pocket, and it looks exactly the same in the full-body view as in the two close views; matching charcoal-grey slim tailored trousers ending at the ankle; plain black leather flat loafers. She carries nothing: no bag, no phone. Her face, skin tone, hair, jewellery and clothes are exactly identical in all three views. This is a studio reference sheet: the plain grey background and neutral white studio light override any scene, night, rain-on-glass or coloured-light instruction that may follow. No text, letters, numbers, labels, captions, arrows, dividing lines, borders, logos or watermarks anywhere in the image.

geography_lock: Right-hand-drive car parked at the left kerb, nose pointing along the road under the flyover. Engine off until b7.
Imran: front right (driver). Tara: rear left (kerb side), diagonal from him, so each sees the other in the rear-view mirror.
Kerb side (car's left): shuttered shop with red and blue neon. Front and right: sodium-orange street lamps. Behind: one dark parked sedan, lights off until b7.

Wipers are still until one sweep in b7.

light_states.rule: Sodium-orange key from the front right through the windscreen; red and blue neon rim from the left windows; deep teal-black shadows. In b4 (profile against the window) neon is strongest and the orange becomes a thin edge on her face.
Base state plus a pale green glow from the keypad phone's blank screen lighting Tara's chin, nose and eye sockets from below. The screen shows no characters.

Hard white headlights from the car behind blast through the rear window: Tara becomes a rim-lit near-silhouette with a white edge on hair and shoulders, raindrops on the rear glass flare, the orange and neon are almost overpowered, her face is held only by faint orange bounce.

prompt_assembly.reference_assets: sheet_prompt, plate_prompt and key_props.prompt are complete prompts. Run them verbatim; do NOT append style_block or negative_rules to them. Generate in generate_order and attach the assets named in pass_refs with -i, in the order listed.
prompt_assembly.shot_frames: Opening line 'Use your image generation tool to create ONE new vertical 9:16 image.' + reference labels by order ('Image 1 is the character reference sheet for Tara; Image 2 is ...; match them exactly') + the shot description (framing, action, expression, light_state rule) + wardrobe_lock for every on-screen character, verbatim + style_block + negative_rules.
prompt_assembly.reference_budget: Codex takes at most 5 reference images. Use one location plate per shot, chosen by camera direction. Typical set: tara sheet, imran sheet (only if he is in frame), one plate, duffel_bag or bag_contents, keypad_phone. Put the lead's sheet first.
prompt_assembly.framing_for_motion: Raw frames are about 941x1672 and are upscaled to 1440x2560, then moved with slow pushes and pans. Keep faces and hands off the outer 6 percent of the frame and out of the bottom fifth, where the app draws subtitles.
prompt_assembly.sheet_gate: Reject and regenerate a sheet if the views do not show the same face, if any view adds jewellery, a bindi, a moustache or text, if Tara's nose stud is on the wrong nostril, or if Imran's rear view is missing.
prompt_assembly.shell_quoting: Prompts contain apostrophes (driver's, viewer's). Pass each prompt to codex as a single argument from a file or a subprocess argument list, never by pasting it inside single quotes.

art_director_notes: The script gives no clothing below the waist, no seat colour and no bag hardware. Those are set here: Tara's charcoal trousers and black loafers, Imran's khaki trousers and sandals, teal-green seat vinyl, brass zip on the bag. Teal vinyl was chosen so the charcoal blazer, maroon blouse and tan bag all separate from the seat under orange light.
The old taxi's door locks are shown as chrome pull-up knobs on the window sills, so the b6 lock is something the picture can show.
Imran's sheet has four views, not three: the rear view is added because most of his shots are of the back of his head.
The fare meter, number plates, permit stickers and neon lettering are removed on purpose: image models garble small text, and garbled text reads as fake.

Nothing in this file has been generated or tested yet. Plates 2 and 3 are written to take plate 1 as a reference; whether Codex holds the cabin across angles is one of the things the proof scene measures.
